name: Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia Nasal Manifestations

criteria.description: Multiple telangiectasias at characteristic sites including nasal mucosa
First-degree relative with HHT according to these criteria
Presence of arteriovenous malformations in lungs, liver, brain, or gastrointestinal tract

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Diagnosis requires at least three major criteria or two major plus two minor criteria
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Nasal mucosal telangiectasias are a key clinical feature contributing to recurrent epistaxis

pathognomonic.notes: Typically begins in childhood or adolescence
Visible dilated capillaries on nasal mucosa

common.notes: Due to repeated bleeding and mucosal irritation
Secondary to mucosal swelling or crusting

common.symptomName: Fatigue related to chronic blood loss
common.notes: May result from iron deficiency anemia

occasional.notes: From repeated trauma or mucosal damage
May be related to anemia or AVMs
Telangiectasias may also affect oral mucosa

rare.symptomName: Nasal deformity from repeated bleeding and scarring
rare.notes: Rare but possible with chronic disease

imaging: CT angiography for AVMs in other organs
genetic: Mutations in ENG, ACVRL1, or SMAD4 genes
other: Visible telangiectasias on nasal mucosa and skin

distinguishingFeatures: No family history of vascular malformations
Localized vascular tumor rather than diffuse telangiectasias

redFlags: Severe recurrent epistaxis causing hemodynamic instability
Evidence of pulmonary or cerebral arteriovenous malformations
Progressive anemia refractory to iron supplementation
references: Shovlin CL. Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia: pathophysiology, diagnosis and treatment. Blood Rev. 2010;24(6):203-219.
Faughnan ME, Palda VA, Garcia-Tsao G, et al. International guidelines for the diagnosis and management of hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia. J Med Genet. 2011;48(2):73-87.
Guttmacher AE, Marchuk DA, White RI Jr. Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia. N Engl J Med. 1995;333(14):918-924.
